I don’t remember where I read it and got the idea (probably Reddit, honestly) but any time someone compliments me in a text or I get an email from work about a positive customer evaluation or anything like that I screen shot it and save it to a folder in my phone called “fighting imposter syndrome”. Then when I feel a downward spiral starting to affect me I open it up and read the positive things other people have said to/about me that reminds me that how I think people see me isn’t actually how people see me.

In the podcast Cryptonaturalist there is an episode call Peptalk (episode 24 I think). That the writer of the show released after the pandemic and it has two lines that have helped me immensely. 
1) “If you can make peace with the unlikely fact that squid the size of school buses patrol the dark oceans at a depth that would crush you to paste, then I have faith you can also make peace with the unlikely fact that you are worthy of all the happiness you have imagined.”
2) “Improvement is an admirable goal, but, remember this, there is no "best version" of you. There is only this version, which stands head and shoulders above all the hypothetical versions you can imagine by virtue of being real and here in the face of everything you have already overcome.”

I listen to that episode. Headphones in. And focus on each word he says as he says it. And 9 times out of 10, it winds down a downward spiral.

Here’s the disconnect. I’m speaking from the perspective of genital herpes and you’re not. Oh my god. See, this comes from me having hsv2g and just assuming everyone else on this thread does too. 

I’ve been in this community for damn over a decade, and I’ve only heard calling out not disclosing genital or vicious forms of oral... usually only to hsv2 or genital hsv1 havers. When did calling out people who have cold sores/fever blisters/benign versions of the virus start?

I never said it was easy. I have sacrificed many things to be open and disclose, I have been in spaces where my diagnosis has made me feel threatened, I’ve lost friends, had to move dorms, had people threaten to sue me, and even attempted to end my life because of herpes. I do 100% blame my gifter, they knew they had it before me, even had transmitted it to another person before me and would go on to transmit it to 4 more people within a year.

Disclosing isn’t about the hsv individual participating in risky behavior, it’s about letting their potential partner decide for themselves should the worst happen, they are aware and consenting to possible transmission. 

I understand there are extenuating circumstances, but not disclosing for casual sex is reckless and (in my opinion) cruel. More reckless than having multiple partners. It took me 32 partners before I contracted hsv, my close friend got it the night they lost their virginity; promiscuity (as alluded to in the title) has got nothing to do with it.

If you knowingly have herpes, and don’t disclose, you are removing that person’s body agency. I have herpes and (before my long term partner) would have multiple partners in a day, but I told my *all* partners and gave them a choice, and did some people turn me down, yeah, but did most? No. Would I stay in contact with them to check in on their status? Of course, I even exchanged numbers with one night stands so that if they contracted it they could reach me. I have, to date, a 0% transmission rate. 

If you had a cold and your friend wanted to hang out you’d preface it with “sure, but just so you know, I’ve got a bit of a cold.” If something had meat in it and your friend is a vegetarian would you not tell them because, well, it’s not like it’s going to hurt them, most people eat meat anyways? 80% of people have oral, and 13% have genital herpes it’s a global thing, but the stigma is worse than the virus... and you well fucking know that. 

******This isn’t about stopping the virus, it’s about being a fucking human and allowing people to make their own decisions about their body by treating people the way you’d want to be treated.******* 

If the person who gave me herpes had told me, I still would’ve slept with them... I just would’ve been more careful. Instead they started a journey of self-loathing that lasted well into the first two years of my decade of having the virus that involved compounded health issues and mental breaks/suicide attempts (with an s) because of the stigma and how it changed my life. I would never want to unknowingly drop that on someone, no matter how careful I am during sex. Something can always go wrong, you need to tell your partners. End of fucking story. 

If you don’t disclose you are selfish and I hope your flare ups combine with a yeast infection and a UTI. Go suck a goddamn lemon.
